=== ARTIFICER FEATURES === 

* Core Artificer Traits • EFotA 7 

* Spellcasting • EFotA 7 
You can channel magical energy through objects. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Artificer spells (Spell DC 16, Spell Attack +8). You can use Thieves' Tools, Tinker's Tools, or another kind of Artisan's Tools as a Spellcasting Focus for your Artificer spells. 

* Tinker’s Magic • EFotA 8 
You know the Mending cantrip. 

As a Magic action while holding Tinker's Tools, you can create one item in an unoccupied space within 5 ft. of yourself, from the provided list. The item lasts until you finish a Long Rest, at which point it vanishes. You can use this feature 5 times per Long Rest. 

   | 5 / Long Rest • 1 Action 

* Replicate Magic Item • EFotA 8 
You have learned arcane plans that you use to make magic items.  

You know 4 Magic Item Plans. 

When you finish a Long Rest, you can create 2 magic items. A magic item created by this feature functions as the normal magic item, except its magic isn't permanent; when you die the magic item vanishes after 1d4 days. If you replace a plan you know with a new plan, any magic item created with the replaced plan immediately vanishes. If an item that you created is a container, and it vanishes, its contents harmlessly appear in and around its space. 

Additionally, you can use any Wand or Weapon created by this feature as a Spellcasting Focus.

least two creatures (one of whom can be yourself), up to a max of 6. Each target receives a magical map, which constantly updates to show the relative position of all the map holders but is illegible to all others. The maps last until you die or until you use this feature again, at which point any existing maps created by this feature immediately vanish. 

While carrying the map, a target gains the following benefits. 

Awareness. The target adds 1d4 to its Initiative rolls. 

Positioning. The target knows the location of all other map holders that are on the same plane of existence as itself. When casting a spell or creating another effect that requires being able to see the effect’s target, a map holder can target another map holder regardless of sight or cover, so long as the other map holder is still within the effect’s range.

* Mapping Magic • EFotA 21 
You gain the following benefits. 

Illuminated Cartography. You can cast Faerie Fire without expending a spell slot, outlining the affected creatures as if in ink. Per Long Rest, you can do 5 time(s). 

Portal Jump. On your turn, you can spend an amount of movement equal to half your Speed (round down) to teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 10 ft. of yourself or within 5 ft. of a creature that is within 30 ft. of you and holding one of your Adventurer’s Atlas maps. You can’t use this benefit if your Speed is 0. 

   | Portal Jump: Special

fields.name: Backstory
fields.default_value:
Ebenezer Tivonhoop was born into a respectable gnomish family where curiosity was encouraged, but usually directed toward practical pursuits. Most of his kin eventually settled into a trade, craft, or profession. Ebenezer never managed to choose just one thing. 

From an early age, he was captivated by questions. Why did kingdoms rise and fall? Who built the ruins scattered across the world? What lay beyond the edges of the maps hanging in scholars' halls? Whenever he found an answer, it only seemed to reveal three new mysteries waiting behind it. 

By the age of eighteen, he had consumed every book he could find near home. Convinced that the world's greatest knowledge lay elsewhere, he packed his belongings and set out to find it. Friends and family expected him to return after a few years. 

Twenty years later, he still hasn't. 

Several years ago, during his travels, Neez met an unusually charismatic Earth Genasi named Rough. The two could not have been more different. Rough chased beauty, stories, and experiences, while Neez chased mysteries, maps, and forgotten knowledge. Despite their differences—or perhaps because of them—they quickly became close friends and travelling companions. He copied manuscripts, repaired mechanisms, catalogued collections, and performed countless odd jobs in exchange for the privilege of spending evenings buried beneath stacks of books and scrolls. 

During these travels, other scholars began calling him "Neez," a shortening of his often-mispronounced first name. The nickname stuck, and these days many people know him only by that name.

fields.name: Appearance
fields.default_value:
- Pale green skin with a healthy, almost luminous tone. 

- Bright yellow-green eyes that are always taking in details—maps, glyphs, gears, anything. 

- Messy dark green hair with a few more strands of silver-green at the temples. 

- Large, expressive ears with a few copper earrings and tiny tools tucked behind them; nicks along the edges from a life of exploration.
